report.summary: Reviewed drift.py chunk 6 of 6 (lines 1401-1550): acceptance application, ignore-drift, refresh, and CLI entry points; claims verified against this chunk; one uncheckable claim noted.
risks: line 1448 | medium | Acceptance matching groups by key, but items with the same key but different kinds are combined; a single acceptance may mask multiple kinds of drift. | Check if DriftItem keys are unique per kind; if not, acceptance semantics may be broader than intended.

line 1455 | medium | Expired acceptance with no matched items adds a STALE_ACCEPTANCE item; but if an expired acceptance matches items, those items get a note and no STALE_ACCEPTANCE is added for the acceptance itself. This may leave the expired acceptance invisible in the report. | Confirm whether an expired acceptance that still matches items is intended to be reported as stale.

line 1464 | medium | Invalid acceptance appends INVALID_ACCEPTANCE and marks matched items with a note, but does not set item.accepted; the item remains blocking. This is consistent with the comment but may be surprising. | Verify intended behavior for items with invalid acceptances.

line 1477 | medium | The ok flag is computed as not any(i.blocking for i in items). If an item is marked accepted but still has blocking=True, the report will be not ok. The code sets item.accepted = True but does not clear blocking. | Check whether accepted items are supposed to have blocking cleared; otherwise acceptance may not unblock the report.

line 1511 | medium | refresh() carries acceptances verbatim from the old snapshot, but does not parse or validate them; invalid acceptances will be carried forward and later flagged. The comment says 'carried forward verbatim' so this is intended, but the risk is that invalid acceptances persist. | Confirm whether refresh should validate or report invalid acceptances.

line 1533 | medium | The CLI's --init path writes a missing snapshot via check(write_missing=True) and then prints the report. If the report is not ok, it still returns 0. This may be intentional for first baseline, but it means a non-green baseline exits 0. | Check whether --init should fail if the initial baseline is not clean.

line 1542 | medium | The CLI's --refresh path always returns 0 after re-baselining, even if the new snapshot is dirty. This is likely intentional, but the risk is that a refresh can silently turn a red run green. | Confirm whether refresh should warn or fail on dirty state.

handoff.purpose: Final chunk: acceptance application, ignore-drift detection, refresh, and CLI entry points.

symbols.name: refresh
symbols.note: Re-baselines the snapshot by scanning and writing a new snapshot with acceptances carried forward verbatim.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: handles --refresh, --init, and default check; returns process exit code.

claims.text: An ABSENT key reads as "nothing was excluded", not as "do not check". Deleting the field must not be a quieter way to narrow the run than setting the variable was.
claims.why: The code sets old_ignore to {"env": "", "file": ""} when the snapshot's 'ignore' is not a dict, and compares it to new_ignore. Thus an absent key is treated as empty ignore, not as a skip.

claims.text: Only ACCEPTABLE_KINDS count as a match. An acceptance still sitting on an island that has since been wired matches a NOW REACHED item, and must go stale rather than quietly ride along on the good news.
claims.why: The code only groups items whose kind is in ACCEPTABLE_KINDS into by_key; acceptances are matched only against those items. If an acceptance matches nothing, it becomes STALE_ACCEPTANCE.

claims.text: Re-baseline. Acceptances are carried forward verbatim -- refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason.
claims.why: refresh() loads the old snapshot, parses acceptances from it, and passes them to write_snapshot without modification. The acceptances are not re-validated or altered.

claims.text: Compare the generated architecture map against the committed snapshot. CI gate, not a pre-commit hook: it parses the whole tree and takes seconds.
claims.why: The claim that it parses the whole tree and takes seconds depends on the scan() implementation, which is not in this chunk. The CLI does call check() which likely calls scan(), but the performance and parsing behavior are not observable here.

claims.text: write the FIRST baseline. Explicit on purpose: a missing snapshot fails, so deleting it is never a green run
claims.why: In the --init branch, if the snapshot file already exists, it prints an error and returns 1. If missing, it calls check(write_missing=True) which presumably writes the baseline; the missing snapshot is not a green run because the first-run path returns 1.

claims.text: Fail CLOSED, matching `daedalus map --check`. This used to write the baseline and exit 0, which made `rm docs/architecture-state.json` a green run through a door reach.py itself classifies as an entry point.
claims.why: After check(), if report.first_run is True, main returns 1. This ensures a missing snapshot fails rather than writing a baseline and exiting 0.

observations.what: Acceptance matching groups by item.key without considering kind, so acceptances with the same key but different kinds are all matched together.
Expired acceptances that still match items only annotate those items; no STALE_ACCEPTANCE is added for the acceptance itself, so the expired acceptance may not be visible in the report.
Invalid acceptances append INVALID_ACCEPTANCE and annotate matched items, but do not set item.accepted; the items remain blocking, consistent with the comment but potentially surprising.
The ok flag is computed as not any(i.blocking for i in items). Accepted items are not explicitly unblocked, so if an item has blocking=True, an acceptance may not make the report green.
refresh() carries acceptances verbatim but does not validate them; invalid acceptances will persist and be flagged later.
The --init path returns 0 even if the initial baseline is not clean (report.render() is printed but return 0 regardless of report.ok).
The --refresh path always returns 0 after re-baselining, even if the new snapshot is dirty.
